topic.title: Displaying Cell Centers and Cell Connections

para.text: Displaying Cell Centers and Cell Connections

While VOROGRIDGEN creates meshes that are close to being Voronoi meshes they are not exactly Voronoi meshes. In a Voronoi mesh, every point in a cell would be closer to the cell center of that cell than to the center of any other cell and the line connecting the centers of neighboring cells would be perpendicular to the boundary between the cells. Often, however, true Voronoi meshes are not ideal for MODFLOW because the line connecting the centers of neighboring cells passes far away from the center of the boundary between the cells or even not pass through the boundary at all.

"For accurate solutions, the standard CVFD formulation requires that a line drawn between the centers of two connected cells should intersect the shared face at a right angle ... . Furthermore, the intersection point should coincide with an appropriate mean position on the shared face" (

If you look hard enough, you can find places where the lines connecting cell centers of neighboring cells are not exactly perpendicular to the boundaries between the cells and also do not quite pass through the middle of the boundary between the cells. The cells at the edge of the model always seem to violate these assumptions to some extent, but interior cells can violate them too, though not severely.
